tei:div.tei:p: “A Prayer for Pentecost” by the Reformed Society of Israelites is found in The Sabbath service and miscellaneous prayers, adopted by the Reformed Society of Israelites, founded in Charleston, S. C., November 21, 1825 (1830), as reprinted by Barnett A. Elzas in The Sabbath Service and Miscellaneous Prayers (1916), pp. 51-52. The prayer does not appear with any further attribution.

The theme of the prayer echoes those of lines from a poem by Goethe, Reinecke Fuchs (1793), which illustrate Pentecost in the context of Spring’s renewal. The opening lines of the poem “speaks of Pentecost as a time of vernal bloom, “idealizing the Pentecost holidays in the German-speaking lands”
In his 1817 poem, Sankt-Rochus-Fest zu Bingen attests to the old German proverb, “Reife Erdbeeren um Pfingsten bedeuten einen guten Wein” (“Ripe strawberries at Pentecost mean a good wine crop”).

tei:note.tei:p: From the article on Pentecost, at [English] Wikipedia).
